item.title: China, EU agree to keep bilateral trade ties stable, hold next meeting in March 2027
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10
China, EU agree to keep bilateral trade ties stable, hold next meeting in March 2027 BEIJING, Oct. 9 (Xinhua) -- China and the European Union (EU) have agreed to maintain stable bilateral economic and trade ties and make them more balanced, while scheduling March 2027 for their next meeting under a trade and investment consultation mechanism, according to a joint statement released Friday. Published by China's Ministry of Commerce, the statement said that Chinese Minister of Commerce Wang Wentao and European Commissioner for Trade and Economic Security Maros Sefcovic jointly chaired the second meeting of the China-EU trade and investment consultation mechanism from Thursday to Friday in Beijing. The two sides engaged in pragmatic and productive discussions and agreed on a list of outcomes, the ministry said. The list set out 16 specific points of consensus covering trade and investment balance, export controls, intellectual property rights and World Trade Organization (WTO) reform. According to the ministry, the two sides agreed to continue exploring the possibility of reducing tariffs on certain goods within the framework of WTO rules. China and the EU reached an understanding on trade in hybrid vehicles in a manner consistent with WTO rules. The two sides will also continue relevant procedures concerning companies' price undertakings and reviews in the EU's anti-subsidy case involving Chinese electric vehicles, the ministry said. The two sides further agreed to hold a technical dialogue on the EU's Foreign Subsidies Regulation. China expressed its willingness to continue facilitating the processing of export license applications for rare earths and permanent magnets destined for the EU through a "green channel" mechanism. The EU, together with its member states, will continue to facilitate the resolution of key licensing cases involving China in the dual-use sector, according to the ministry. The two sides also agreed to explore investment cooperation to promote their respective economic development and discussed future-oriented cooperation. As key trading partners, China and the EU reaffirmed their commitment to properly handling their differences within the framework of WTO rules, and to keeping bilateral economic and trade ties stable and making them more balanced, the ministry noted. The two sides also agreed to hold the third meeting of the consultation mechanism in March next year and maintain close communication in the meantime, including through a ministerial video conference in January next year, the ministry said. Both sides viewed the second meeting as a new starting point for deepening China-EU cooperation and tasked their working teams with advancing follow-up work, promoting the early implementation of the agreed outcomes, and preparing for the third meeting of the China-EU trade and investment consultation mechanism, according to the ministry. item.title: Symposium held to study Xi's works on culture
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10
Symposium held to study Xi's works on culture Li Shulei, a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and head of the Publicity Department of the CPC Central Committee, attends and addresses a symposium held to study the first and second volumes of selected works on culture by Xi Jinping, general secretary of the CPC Central Committee, in Beijing, capital of China, Oct. 9, 2026. (Xinhua/Wang Ye) BEIJING, Oct. 9 (Xinhua) -- A symposium was held in Beijing on Friday to study the first and second volumes of selected works on culture by Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee. Li Shulei, a member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and head of the Publicity Department of the CPC Central Committee, attended the symposium and delivered a speech. The volumes were published in August by the Central Party Literature Press. Attendees at the symposium said the selections systematically present the fundamental principles, core content and essential requirements of Xi Jinping Thought on Culture, providing an authoritative textbook for its study and application. In studying the selections, it is important to consciously study and apply Xi Jinping Thought on Culture and better fulfill the cultural mission of the new era, they said. The attendees called for efforts to gain a deeper understanding of Xi Jinping Thought on Culture as the fundamental guidelines for public communication and cultural work in the new era, as well as its strategic vision for building China into a leading country in culture. They also urged efforts to translate the gains from studying it into concrete actions. Organized by the Publicity Department of the CPC Central Committee, the symposium was attended by officials from relevant central departments, central publicity and cultural institutions, and publicity departments of provincial-level CPC committees, as well as experts and scholars in social sciences. The volumes of the selected works contain 78 pieces of the most important and fundamental works by Xi on cultural development from November 2012 to February 2026, featuring reports, speeches, letters and instructions. Xi Jinping Thought on Culture was formally put forward at a national meeting on the work of public communication and culture in October 2023. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. item.title: China records 826 mln domestic tourist trips during 2026 National Day holiday amid diverse offerings
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10
China records 826 mln domestic tourist trips during 2026 National Day holiday amid diverse offerings Tourists view a giant floral basket installation at Tian'anmen Square in Beijing, capital of China, Oct. 1, 2026. China recorded 826 million domestic tourist trips during the seven-day National Day holiday, with tourism spending totaling 738.38 billion yuan (about 109.67 billion U.S. dollars), the Ministry of Culture and Tourism said Friday. On a daily average basis, the number of domestic trips rose 6.3 percent from the eight-day National Day and Mid-Autumn Festival holiday in 2025, while tourism spending increased 4.3 percent, according to the ministry. (Xinhua/Ju Huanzong) BEIJING, Oct. 9 (Xinhua) -- China saw 826 million domestic tourist trips during the recent seven-day National Day holiday, with tourism spending totaling 738.38 billion yuan (about 109.67 billion U.S. dollars), the Ministry of Culture and Tourism said on Friday. On a daily average basis, the number of domestic trips rose 6.3 percent from the eight-day National Day and Mid-Autumn Festival holiday in 2025, while tourism spending increased 4.3 percent, according to the ministry. The holiday witnessed a vibrant cultural scene, with 180 large-scale performances held nationwide, including 125 concerts and 55 music festivals. Beyond cultural performances, the integration of tourism with culture, commerce and sports continued to deepen. Mass-participation sports events and digital innovations offered visitors new experiences and helped drive tourism-related consumption. Meanwhile, around 40 percent of tourists visited revolutionary sites or took part in activities such as flag-raising ceremonies and patriotic performances. This trend takes on added significance this year, which marks the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March (1934-1936). The arduous journey helped lay the foundation for the eventual victory of the Chinese revolution. Dai Bin, president of the China Tourism Academy, said the flow of visitors to revolutionary landmarks reflects people's emotional identification with revolutionary traditions. When they travel, they don't just want to see history. They also want to draw deeper inspiration from the revolutionary legacy for their lives today, Dai noted. Measures to boost tourism consumption have also helped expand holiday options for visitors and enhance their travel experiences. Under a nationwide cultural and tourism consumption campaign running from late September through October, local authorities have organized a variety of activities and distributed more than 310 million yuan in consumption subsidies. item.title: China issues guidelines on developing new quality productive forces
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10
China issues guidelines on developing new quality productive forces BEIJING, Oct. 9 (Xinhua) -- The Communist Party of China Central Committee and the State Council have issued a set of guidelines aimed at accelerating the development of new quality productive forces to bolster high-quality development. These guidelines outline 19 key measures in five areas, namely advancing scientific and technological innovation, deepening the integration of sci-tech and industrial innovation, innovating development approaches, promoting institutional and mechanism innovation, and improving mechanisms for talent development. Noting that developing new quality productive forces is an intrinsic requirement and an important focus of promoting high-quality development, these guidelines stress the importance of innovation-driven development, reform and measures tailored to local conditions, and following the approach of "establishing the new before abolishing the old." The guidelines call for pursuing high technology, high efficiency and high quality, properly handling the relationships between the government and the market, between the qualitative nature of productive forces and the forms they take in industry and business, between reform and development, and between self-reliance and opening up, while coordinating development and security. "The new round of scientific and technological revolution and industrial transformation has opened up broad prospects for developing new quality productive forces. Seizing this historic opportunity requires moving faster to achieve greater self-reliance and strength in science and technology and raising innovation capacity across the board to maintain strategic initiative," said Wang Shengxiao, a researcher with the Party School of the Communist Party of China Central Committee. The guidelines call for stronger original and transformative sci-tech innovation, with major sci-tech projects to focus on strategic, landmark and leading products, targeting the cutting-edge of global science and technology and serving major areas of economic development, major national needs, and people's health. They stress the need for faster breakthroughs in key core technologies, including efforts to promote the high-quality development of key manufacturing industrial chains and implement industrial innovation projects in priority areas. The guidelines emphasize coordinated efforts to strengthen national strategic sci-tech capabilities, giving full play to national laboratories in organizing major national sci-tech projects and building major innovation platforms. The guidelines also urge optimizing the roles and distribution of national sci-tech research institutions, high-level research universities and leading sci-tech enterprises. The guidelines underline the principal role of enterprises in sci-tech innovation, encouraging technology-based small and medium-sized enterprises to increase research and development investment and supporting capable private enterprises in taking the lead in major national technological breakthrough tasks. To speed up the transformation of sci-tech achievements into real productive forces, the guidelines call for leveraging the advantages of China's vast market to better connect technology with the market and advance the development of new quality productive forces on a larger scale. The guidelines also urge upgrading traditional industries through the application of digital, intelligent and green technologies. The country should seek to advance producer services toward greater specialization and the higher end of the value chain, while improving the quality, diversity and convenience of consumer services, according to the guidelines. For emerging industries, the guidelines emphasize efforts to foster their growth and develop new pillar industries. The guidelines encourage greater cross-industry and cross-regional integration, measures to avoid "involution-style" competition, and support eastern regions to help central, western and northeastern regions develop emerging industries in line with local conditions. The guidelines call for forward-looking planning for future industries and emphasize the need to make full use of existing fiscal policies to support their development and guide social capital to steadily increase investment. The guidelines also urge promoting the deep integration of the digital economy and the real economy, optimizing the layout, construction and operation of national data infrastructure, advancing the digital transformation of the manufacturing sector, and building digital industrial clusters with international competitiveness. The guidelines call for fully implementing the "AI Plus" initiative, using artificial intelligence (AI) to transform traditional industries, accelerating innovation in AI and other digital and intelligent technologies, and promoting the widespread application of AI across industries. Efforts are also needed to establish systems for technology monitoring, early risk warning and emergency response to ensure that AI is safe, reliable and controllable, the guidelines note. These guidelines further propose building a green, low-carbon and circular economic system by strengthening green manufacturing, developing green services, expanding the green energy industry, and driving the supply of green products via green consumption. Efforts should be made to optimize the policy toolbox for green development and implement fiscal, financial, investment, pricing, technological and environmental policies that promote green and low-carbon development, according to the guidelines. The country will actively advance the energy revolution and accelerate the green transition of energy use in production and daily life across society, the guidelines add. The guidelines call for deepening reform to promote close integration of science and technology with the economy, saying that efforts should be made to build an open, shared and secure nationally integrated data market. The guidelines also stress the need to improve the market regulation system and increase the supply of innovative financial products. The guidelines pledge to allocate advanced production factors globally by expanding high-standard opening up and actively building a global innovation cooperation network, and encouraging foreign venture capital institutions, international standards organizations and others to develop in China. The guidelines urge cultivating talent urgently needed for the development of new quality productive forces, adding that policies on the use and flow of talent should be improved. "New quality productive forces are primarily driven by transformational technological breakthroughs, which bring profound changes to how innovation is organized, industries evolve and resources are allocated," said Liu Zhenzhong, a researcher at the Institute of Industrial and Technological Economics of the National Development and Reform Commission. "These changes require deeper reforms to reshape institutional frameworks and remove obstacles to development." The outline of the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) identifies the development of new quality productive forces as a key strategic task and sets out 28 major projects related to this goal, accounting for 25.7 percent of the 109 major projects outlined in the plan. The projects focus on four priorities: strengthening industrial capabilities and competitiveness, fostering emerging industries, pursuing breakthroughs in cutting-edge technologies, and enhancing innovation capabilities. At an international seminar held in Beijing in September, Chinese experts said China's development of new quality productive forces could provide fresh momentum for global economic growth and create new opportunities for countries at different stages of modernization. Abdulrahman Bello Dambazau, Nigeria's ambassador to China, noted that the emphasis on talent development, scientific research and industrial upgrading could offer useful reference for developing countries. China's development of high-tech, green and intelligent industries is also creating more opportunities for cross-border investment and industrial cooperation. At the China International Fair for Investment and Trade in September, representatives from European countries explored cooperation with China in areas such as clean energy, AI, smart manufacturing, biomedicine and the digital economy. item.title: Japan urged to severely punish perpetrator of Chinese embassy break-in: spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-09
Japan urged to severely punish perpetrator of Chinese embassy break-in: spokesperson BEIJING, Oct. 8 (Xinhua) -- China once again urges the Japanese side to impose severe punishment on the perpetrator who broke into the Chinese Embassy in Japan with a knife to serve as a warning to others, foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said on Thursday. Mao made the remarks at a regular media briefing while answering a question regarding the first court hearing in the trial of Kodai Murata, a former Japan Self-Defense Forces (SDF) officer accused of forcibly entering the Chinese Embassy in Japan. It is an egregious incident unprecedented in the international community that an active-duty officer of Japan's SDF broke into the Chinese Embassy in Japan with a knife and made violent threats against Chinese diplomatic personnel, Mao said. She said it constitutes a serious violation of the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, poses grave threats to the personal safety of Chinese diplomatic staff and the security of the diplomatic premises, and lays bare a host of deep-seated problems in Japan, including rampant right-wing forces and inadequate management and discipline of SDF personnel. "Whether Japan can handle the case seriously in accordance with law will test whether the Japanese government earnestly fulfills its obligations under international law, and bears on the country's national credibility and international image," Mao said. item.title: China warns Philippines to cease provocations, false claims
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-09
China warns Philippines to cease provocations, false claims BEIJING, Oct. 8 (Xinhua) -- The China Coast Guard (CCG) on Thursday warned the Philippine side to immediately stop its infringements, provocations and false claims after a Philippine Coast Guard vessel transported an injured person from a grounded vessel near Ren'ai Jiao. Jiang Lue, a spokesperson for the CCG, said that on Thursday, Philippine Coast Guard vessel 4409 went to waters near Ren'ai Jiao to transport one injured person from the vessel illegally grounded there. Out of humanitarian considerations, the Chinese side immediately allowed the Philippine side to transfer the injured person by small boat, and the CCG handled the matter in accordance with the law and regulations, and provided necessary assistance, Jiang said. The Philippine side's relevant remarks disregard the facts and distort the truth in an attempt to mislead the public, Jiang added. China has indisputable sovereignty over the Nansha Qundao, including Ren'ai Jiao, and the adjacent waters, he noted. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: Strong demand in China boosts US exporters
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-09
Strong demand in China boosts US exporters China's growing appetite for high-quality consumer goods and industrial inputs is drawing more products from the United States into its market, as holiday spending, industrial upgrading and the recent reciprocal tariff-cut arrangement offer US exporters more room to expand sales in the country, according to trade experts and business leaders. From fresh fruit and seafood to integrated circuits and energy products, US shipments to China have remained substantial, reflecting the complementary nature of the two economies and the potential for expanding imports to support more balanced and mutually beneficial bilateral trade, they said. The trend was particularly visible during the National Day holiday from Oct 1 to Wednesday, as stronger demand for food and other consumer products prompted Chinese importers to step up purchases from overseas suppliers. Oheng Supply Chain Management (Ningbo) Co, a cross-border food products importer based in Ningbo, Zhejiang province, imported 44.62 million yuan ($6.66 million) worth of products, including fresh cherries and fish oil from the US, in the first eight months of 2026. Ahead of the holiday, shipments of US fish oil, red yeast rice, fresh cherries and grapes purchased by the company arrived in China to replenish supplies for the holiday market. "The US is one of our main sources for products such as fish oil and cherries, with stable supply capacity," said Zhou Shouming, the company's director of customs affairs. "Judging from our sales, domestic consumers' demand for high-quality imported food continues to grow." In late September, China and the US released reciprocal tariff-cut lists covering about $30 billion worth of imports from each side. Zhou said the arrangement will lower costs for products including fresh cherries and grapes and give the company greater flexibility in pricing, allowing it to bring more high-quality US food products to Chinese buyers. Pistachios are also included on China's tariff-cut list. Nut growers in California are expected to export 111,000 metric tons of pistachios to China in the 2026 crop year (Sept 1, 2026 to Aug 31, 2027), according to Wonderful Pistachios & Almonds, the largest pistachio producer by production volume and sales revenue in the US. Anita Lam, managing director for China at Wonderful Pistachios, said the industry remains confident about the long-term growth potential for California pistachios in the Chinese market, adding that her company will continue to leverage its vertically integrated supply chain and long-standing operations to deepen its presence in the country. Demand for fresh seafood has also been strong in China. Imports of US lobsters through Ningbo Lishe International Airport were valued at 200 million yuan between January and August, surging 468.5 percent year-on-year, according to Ningbo Customs. Li Yongguo, president of Hengsheng Supply Chain (Dongguan) Co, a Dongguan, Guangdong province-based trading company, said that beyond food products, China's demand for imported integrated circuits has continued to grow, fueled by the expansion of artificial intelligence infrastructure and rising demand from the country's electronics manufacturing sector. The Chinese company imported 10.31 billion yuan worth of integrated circuits from the US in the first three quarters, up 74.2 percent year-on-year, statistics from Huangpu Customs in Guangdong showed. Miao Yingchun, a researcher at Wuhan University's Institute for International Studies in Wuhan, Hubei province, said China's demand for US products is being driven by both consumption and production — consumers seeking a wider range of quality goods and manufacturers requiring raw materials, components and equipment. Wang Huiyao, president of the Beijing-based think tank Center for China and Globalization, noted that the Chinese and US economies are deeply interconnected. "If the two countries can expand tariff reductions in specific areas and establish effective trade and investment mechanisms, even relatively limited steps at the outset could help strengthen confidence and pave the way for broader cooperation," he said. China-US trade rose 5.5 percent year-on-year to $400.84 billion during the January-to-August period, while China's imports from the US grew 3.4 percent year-on-year, data from the General Administration of Customs showed. The resilience of bilateral trade is also reflected in recent research. China's expanding import market continues to offer opportunities for US companies despite shifts in global trade and persistent bilateral economic tensions, according to a new report released in Los Angeles that examines changes in US exports to China and the broader impact of the China International Import Expo. The report, "The Evolution of the Structure of US Exports to China and the Extended Effects Index from a CIIE Perspective (2026)", was released earlier this week at the Bridge to Shanghai: Business Opportunities with China event, part of an overseas outreach series ahead of the ninth CIIE, which will be held in Shanghai from Nov 5 to 10. The report said the composition of trade also points to continuing economic complementarity between the world's two largest economies. It identifies China as the largest overseas market for US soybeans and cotton in 2026, and an important market for US integrated circuits and medical devices. It also said the US remains a major source of China's services imports and has maintained a surplus in bilateral services trade. Those patterns, according to the researchers, underscore the enduring commercial ties between the two economies even as tariffs, technology restrictions and changes in global sourcing have altered the bilateral trade landscape. Li Qingjuan, director of the Think Tank Center at Fudan University's Fudan International School of Finance, said the CIIE is no longer simply about bringing products into the Chinese market. Instead, it has evolved into a global platform for companies to showcase their products, connect with potential partners and explore business opportunities. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. item.title: Flame for Changchun 2027 Winter Universiade lit in Turin
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-09
Flame for Changchun 2027 Winter Universiade lit in Turin Mayor of Changchun Gu Gang (2nd L) and president of FISU Leonz Eder (1st L) jointly light the cauldron with the torch from the first World University Games in Turin in 1959 during the flame collection ceremony for the Changchun 2027 Winter Universiade in Turin, Italy, Oct. 8, 2026. (Xinhua/Wang Kaiyan) TURIN, Italy, Oct. 9 (Xinhua) -- The flame for the Changchun 2027 Winter Universiade was lit Thursday in Turin, Italy, where the first World University Games were held in 1959, beginning its journey to China ahead of the January event. Changchun Mayor Gu Gang and International University Sports Federation President Leonz Eder jointly lit a cauldron using a torch from the inaugural Games before transferring the flame to a lantern for the Changchun Games. The lantern was carried through central Turin from the University of Turin to the Polytechnic University of Turin, passing the Egyptian Museum along the way. Gu expressed hope that the flame would symbolize friendship and that winter sports would promote cultural exchanges between East and West, fostering mutual understanding among young people worldwide. A welcoming ceremony for the flame is scheduled for October 14 in Changchun, according to the Games' organizing committee. The Winter Universiade will run from January 15 to 25, 2027. Eder recently told Xinhua that preparations were progressing smoothly and expressed confidence that the Games would attract a record number of participating delegations. item.title: Qingdao Port keeps expanding its global shipping services
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-09
Qingdao Port keeps expanding its global shipping services A drone photo taken on Oct. 8, 2026 shows cargo ships docking at Qingdao Port in Qingdao, east China's Shandong Province. As an international shipping hub in Northeast Asia, Qingdao Port has been expanding its shipping network, adding 16 foreign trade routes so far this year. The port now operates nearly 240 foreign trade routes, connecting over 700 ports in over 180 countries and regions.
